coordinates.locator: JUNO physics and detector paper (arXiv:2104.02565), Sec. 1.2
coordinates.note: Published coordinate converted from degrees-minutes-seconds. Kept approximate: against the GPS-surveyed baselines of the same paper, the six Yangjiang reactor buildings in OpenStreetMap sit about 100 m farther from this point than published (Taishan agrees to 10–16 m), so either the point or the tracing is off by ~100 m.
coordinates.quote: The geographic location is 112° 31’05” E and 22° 07’05” N.

depth.quote: The experimental hall, spanning more than 50 meters, is under a granite mountain of over 700 m overburden.

depth_mwe.note: Consistent with the 700 m granite-rock depth on file (granite density ~2.6 g/cm³ implies ~1800 m.w.e.).
depth_mwe.quote: The detector is located in a shallow underground laboratory with an overburden of 1800 m.w.e.

muon_flux.note: A simulated expectation, not a measurement: a simulation taking the surveyed mountain profile into account, for a vertical overburden of 693.35 m (1800 m.w.e.) at the detector centre; average muon energy 207 GeV; no uncertainty given. 0.004 Hz/m^2 is 0.004 m^-2 s^-1. The 2015 yellow book (arXiv:1507.05613) gave 0.0030 Hz/m^2 and 215 GeV; the 2021 paper says the hall was later shifted by about 60 m. No JUNO measurement of the cosmic-muon flux was found.
muon_flux.quote: The muon rate and average energy in the JUNO detector are 0.004 Hz/m2 and 207 GeV estimated by simulation, taking the surveyed mountain profile into account.

name: JUNO underground experimental hall, Dashi Hill, Kaiping
notes: The underground experimental hall itself is reported as 'spanning more than 50 meters' (CDR) with a total civil-construction volume around 300,000 m³ and a main hall of about 120,000 m³ (per a secondary IHEP-related search summary, not checked against a primary source).

summary.plain: The rock cavern under Dashi Hill near Kaiping, in Jiangmen, southern China, where the JUNO neutrino detector sits, shielded by more than 700 metres of granite.
summary.technical: Underground experimental hall of facility:juno-jiangmen, excavated beneath Dashi Hill near Kaiping, Jiangmen, Guangdong, with over 700 m of granite overburden, 52.5-53 km from the Yangjiang and Taishan nuclear power plants.
